sense.text:
“Blessed be the Lord, who daily loadeth us with benefits, even the God of our salvation.” When we hear benefits we might think of it in a worldly sense, but the Lord loads us with the things that benefit us to remain in this truth, to strive in this truth, to gain wisdom and understanding and to grow. That is why in our prayers we bless the Lord and bless his holy name: because every single day he loads us with benefits.

These are not the benefits of this world. We ain’t talking about Aetna, Aflac or Blue Cross Blue Shield, and we’re not talking about your 401k. In this oppressive captivity we’ve got headaches, heartache, backache and stress, and the Lord says, I have something that’s going to benefit you every single day. All of us should take advantage of that.

precepts.why:
When the multitudes came out against Christ with swords and staves, he said to them, “I sat daily with you teaching in the temple.” Daily. Here it is: the Lord loads us with benefits daily, and we read of his son, the Messiah, Jesus the Christ, teaching daily in the temple, loading the people with the Lord’s benefits.

Learning these things daily is a benefit from God. Always keep that in mind.

“All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness”. All scripture is beneficial. The Lord, who loads us with benefits daily, loads us with all scripture because it is profitable. Instruction in righteousness can only benefit us as a people, collectively, individually and communally.

“That the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works.” What better benefit is there than perfection? The benefit is that all your works may be good and profitable, and that you yourself may be perfect.

Everything this world calls a benefit has stipulations. Get into an accident and the insurance company cancels your policy and sends you looking for some other insurance. The benefits God loads us with every day have no such stipulations.

sense.text:
You could have been anywhere else this morning, but you’re here. “If any man will come after me, let him deny himself”: if anyone desires to follow Christ, the pinnacle of priorities is to deny yourself. Deny all the desires you may have, especially in unrighteousness, that hold you back from coming into the truth or from growing in the truth. Whatever could be a stumbling block for you, friends, family, goods, a job, whatever it is, you must be ready to deny it, because you cannot serve two masters. All of your lust, all of your desires, all the stuff that holds you back from coming into Christ, from progressing and growing, or as the scripture says, abounding, has to be put aside in order to fully follow Christ.

“And take up his cross daily”. The Lord loads us with benefits daily, Christ was in the temple teaching us daily, all scripture is profitable to make us perfect, and Christ says that to follow him who teaches us daily, you must take up your cross daily. The cross is your burden, and it is also what you are willing to lose for the gospel’s sake, whether it’s livelihood, home, goods or your life. That is the weight you must take up and carry every single day, and then you will be able to follow Christ.

precepts.why: “My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation.” Christ just said, if any man will come after me; the Wisdom of Sirach says, if thou come to serve the Lord. And to prepare your soul for temptation is to take up your cross. It’s saying the same exact thing.

With the burden we have to carry, it benefits us to hang on to the teaching, the blessing the Lord loads us with every single day, with our lives. Hang on to it with your life, because what else have you got? Some folks are storing up backup plans and contingency plans: if they correct me about this, I might go back into the world and do that.

Paul says, “I die daily.” The cross you take up daily and the teaching you need to sustain you daily allow you to kill off that old man daily. That is a daily process that has to happen in order for you to follow Christ.

“But sin, taking occasion by the commandment, wrought in me all manner of concupiscence.” Wrought in me, worked in me, all manner of evil sexual desires. Paul is very open in the things he battled with, and many of us should be the same.

This is why we must die daily and take up the cross: shedding the things that weigh you down lets you walk better in this truth. Picture a man or woman carrying a bunch of baggage, and each bag is something you’re hanging on to: your lust, your stuff, your hatred, whatever it is. The more you get rid of, the longer your endurance, the longer you can walk and travel, and the more you can actually help others. If your hands are full of weights that have been weighing you down, how can you be a help to anyone else? You can’t help yourself. Shedding those things is for your benefit.

“For without the law sin was dead. For I was alive without the law once: but when the commandment came, sin revived, and I died.” Paul said in 1 Corinthians 15 that he died daily. He is not saying he was physically killed every single day. The sin within his sinful flesh, that man, he had to kill every single day, because his desire was to follow Christ.

“Nevertheless the foundation of God standeth sure, having this seal, The Lord knoweth them that are his. And, Let every one that nameth the name of Christ depart from iniquity.” Everyone that names the name of Christ, that desires to follow Christ, has to deny himself, and here it says he must depart from iniquity. So what is the self you have to deny? It’s the sins that are within you.

The job, the stuff, all those things you have to detach from are things we can set up as idols. How could your job be an idol? When you choose to break the Sabbath day for your job. You know it’s the Lord’s Sabbath day, but you need to order those new rims for your car real quick, so you buy anyway: you idolize your stuff. We have to deny that sin within us in order to follow Christ.

All of this is the price of gold. Not Fort Knox, not the white man’s gold sitting in a safe. Take that out of your mind.

sense.text:
“I will not be burdensome to you: for I seek not yours, but you”. Paul had to deal with the Corinthians on numerous levels. He was very open with them about what he was dealing with, in order to win them over. As you read in Acts, many of the Corinthians believed, but there was still a fraction of negroes in the church of Corinth that Paul always had to check, reprimand and get on about various things, because of the way they dealt with him as the elder over the congregation. They always questioned him about what he was doing with the alms that came in.

Paul says, I’m not burdensome to you, because I don’t need your stuff, I don’t need your baggage. What I need is you. You’re what the Lord wants.

“Though the more abundantly I love you, the less I be loved.” The more love Paul showed the Corinthians, the less love he received. It is written to the Corinthians, but it’s an open letter to us all. Always remember that: it ain’t just for the church of Corinth, he’s talking to all of us to this day.

“Nevertheless, being crafty, I caught you with guile.” Guile is skill in achieving one’s end through indirect, subtle or underhanded means. It is also deception, the inclination or practice of misleading others through lies or trickery. Paul told the church of Corinth, I caught you in the practice of misleading others through lies or trickery.

In order to follow Christ there are things we have to deny within ourselves. You may have never killed anyone, never beat anyone up, never had a fight a day in your life, but you’ve got that gift of gab to get over on your people. We say we would never fall for a scam, but brothers and sisters fall for things like this all the time, overtly and covertly: can I come stay with you for a while? And they post up and never leave. That is guile, that is trickery, coming in with ulterior motives.

We talk about beating each other up, robbing, stealing, killing and adultery, but these subtle things must be purged from us as well. Paul taught the church of Corinth himself and caught them in it, so it is not something in the scriptures we don’t deal with. How much more today, with all these distractions and devices? Pathological liars, habitual liars, lying about small things and big things, and when they get caught they try to make it like you’re the problem. Even people in the world are talking about it. Among our people is the same spirit Paul caught in Corinth.

“Being born again”: there are some things you did before coming into the truth, but now, being born again, it shouldn’t be so. Some think a lie is not a big deal, it’s just a white lie. I don’t know why you would even compare it to white. A lie is a lie, and Paul had to deal with it because it causes schisms, division in the body.

“Not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, by the word of God”. The word we more commonly use for being born again is repenting. Before repenting we all were a corruptible seed; after repenting we are now incorruptible seed. And how did that happen? By the word of God: the word God loads us with daily, the benefit Christ taught in the temple daily, which causes us to die daily in order to follow him. The word of God is what makes that transition.

“For all flesh is as grass”. Our life is as simple as a blade of grass that can be plucked up and blown away in the wind. We can be leaving here, coming here, going to work, going about our day, and in an instant our life can be snatched up just like that.

“But the word of the Lord endureth for ever. And this is the word which by the gospel is preached unto you.” What endures forever is the word of the Lord, and it is preached to you, available to you, daily. The word of the Lord is there to be a benefit to you every single day. If you don’t use those benefits, shame on you.

precepts.why:
“Wherefore laying aside all malice, and all guile, and hypocrisies, and envies, and all evil speakings, As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word”. As newborn babes: in chapter one it was called being born again, and Peter touches on it again here. As newborn babes, as those who are born again, desire the sincere milk of the word, “that ye may grow thereby”.

The process of repenting is through the word of God, and growing while here is through the word of God too. It is not a process that stops after you’ve come into the truth. I don’t care if you’ve been in the truth ten years, all of us should see it as: I still have some growing to do.

sense.text:
“Let him refrain his tongue from evil, and his lips that they speak no guile”. We often use this chapter for marriage, but Peter, the elder, the bishop of the church, is writing an open letter to us all. We just read about guile, about lying, about dealing falsely one with another, so if we want to see good days we must refrain our mouths from evil. The guile we were in when we were corruptible, before repentance, is the old man we have to deny in order to grow and to see better days.

That process has to sink in, because we so easily forget it once trials happen, tribulation happens, you’re in an emotional state and things don’t go your way. Israel’s issue has never really been knowing the commandments of God. It has always been applying the commandments of God. That’s our hiccup, our shortcoming. The tribulation is going to come, and if you don’t know the process before that bump in the road, when that thing happens you’re going to suffer and fall.

“Let him eschew evil, and do good; let him seek peace, and ensue it.” The only way our condition changes is when you eschew evil: turn from the wicked ways you were in, forsake them and follow the Lord. It’s just that simple.

“For the eyes of the Lord are over the righteous, and his ears are open unto their prayers”. The righteous who love life, in the sense that they follow the ways of the Lord, the Lord hears their prayers.

“But the face of the Lord is against them that do evil.” If you are repented, born again, a newborn babe, and you’re still in the midst of the things you were in, the old man, the corruptible man, and not working on it, the Lord is actually fighting against you. I don’t know if anybody’s arms are long enough to box with God on that one.

“But let none of you suffer as a murderer, or as a thief, or as an evildoer, or as a busybody in other men’s matters.” The evil speaking and guile were highlighted, but it goes into all the sins. Peter expounds: there should be no guile in your mouth for evil speaking, and none of you should be a murderer, a thief, an evildoer, or a busybody in other people’s business.

Evil speaking is like a pebble thrown in a lake: the rippling goes out very far. You speak evil and it causes division, confusion, an uproar of the city. The other sins ripple out the same way.

precepts.why:
A lot of us say, I ain’t stab nobody today, I ain’t shoot nobody, I ain’t choke nobody out. Peter is talking about physical murder, but here’s the deeper meaning: “Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer”. It’s almost like a deep mystery. Lord, I didn’t kill nobody, but I hate his black gums, I hate his black neck. That’s what God says: you’re a murderer.

So to suffer as a murderer is also to be found hating your brother or your sister, and that should not be in any of us.

sense.text: “Walk in love, as Christ also hath loved us, and hath given himself for us an offering and a sacrifice to God”. Christ gave himself for us, the ultimate sacrifice.

“But fornication, and all uncleanness, or covetousness, let it not be once named among you”. Peter highlighted evil speaking, murderers and thieves; now Paul highlights other things. There has been an uptick in fornication in the body. In order to follow Christ you must put away those lustful desires, because we are an organized nation that encourages and builds godly marriages. As we read in 1 Peter 3, if a marriage or union is done uprightly, God has his ears open to your prayers, but his face is against them that do evil. So when it’s hell on earth at home, know that the Lord is actually fighting against your marriage. He made it very clear in his word.

Not once named among you. The church of Ephesus should have had no issue with fornication, and Israel United in Christ should have no fornication, because we are the church of the Lord, the congregation of the Lord, the people of God, and God has loaded us daily with the understanding of how marriage should work. But some say the Bishop, who has been in the truth over thirty years studying this Bible intricately, with the spirit obviously on him, doesn’t know what he’s talking about, and go do what they’re going to do with a sister. Isn’t that what we were doing before we were born again, before we were newborn babes? So where is the change?

“As becometh saints”: you have to do saintly things. Put away the evil speaking. Deny yourself, as Christ said: the urges you’ve always had as a man, or always had as a woman, are a part of the self you have to deny, and he gives us his word, his teachings, every single day to help us through those things. Some things will take longer to overcome than others. Paul battled with concupiscence, but he made sure he labored more than every other apostle. With as much work as has to be done in this truth, how do you find time to sit down and watch porn every single day? It means you ain’t got enough to do, you ain’t putting enough bricks, you ain’t laboring, you’re not studying enough.

Covetousness too should not be named among us. Often when Bishop Nathanyel and the Bishops visit the congregations, the congregations want to present them with gifts, and Bishop Nathanyel has said he appreciates it, but what he would prefer above all is a sinless congregation. Which one of us is going to stand up and say, I’m going to do what the Bible says? You came through these doors because of what the Bible says; how do you come through the doors now and say you’re not going to do what the Bible says?

“Neither filthiness”. Brothers, stop trying to lay with your wives, and sisters, stop letting your husbands lay with you, when you’re still in the cycle of your menstrual. That’s filthy.

The Lord is using the apostles and the prophets to touch on every single sin Israel commits. People in the world are talking about liars, covetousness, hatred and envy, so why are we in here talking about it? Because we have not become newborn babes, we have not been born again. These are things deep within us that we have to labor to deny.

“For this ye know, that no whoremonger, nor unclean person, nor covetous man, who is an idolater, hath any inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and of God.” You’re born again, a newborn babe, repented, and you come in doing the same thing you did before, because you’ve done it so often for so long it became normal, and you say the Lord don’t see me, he didn’t punish me yet. The Lord says you’re going to cost yourself everlasting life, a kingdom that is already set up for you.

Refusing what is required to get that kingdom is saying: I like being a slave, I like being on the bottom, I like having eggs thrown and words written on my house like they did LeBron James, I like being oppressed, I like going to my enemy for the want of every dang thing. You and your wife lay down and create a baby, you watch that child come out, and you have to go to the white man for a birth certificate to say that’s your child. You like depending on them for everything? The only way that changes is when you turn from the wicked ways you were in, forsake them and follow the Lord.

“I have brought unto thee my son, which hath a dumb spirit”: a dumb spirit, meaning unable to speak. The father gives the attributes of what his son deals with: “he teareth him: and he foameth, and gnasheth with his teeth, and pineth away”. He foams at the mouth, he grinds his teeth, he pines away, like a person scratching at a tree or a wall.

Today you would call that schizophrenia, but the father called it a dumb spirit. There are different spectrums of schizophrenia. Schizophreniform disorder is having the symptoms of schizophrenia for a period of one to six months: delusions, hallucinations, disorganized speech, odd behaviors, lack of energy and social withdrawal. A lot of times we say, I’m an introvert, which is a social disorder. It is part of the schizophrenia spectrum and can be an early sign of it. It affects men and women equally, but it usually develops at a younger age in men, and it can happen very quickly. And here a man came to Christ about his son.

“Straightway the spirit tare him; and he fell on the ground, and wallowed foaming.” As the young brother is on the ground foaming at the mouth, Christ asks the father, “How long is it ago since this came unto him? And he said, Of a child.” This is very important. Schizophreniform starts in men at a younger age.

The spirits we’ve been going over, the hatred, the evil concupiscence, the sexual sins, the lying, some of those spirits have been on you since you were a child. A lot of the evil concupiscence you lust after now is because you found your daddy’s or your mama’s porn stash when you were a little kid. You were exposed at a very young age, and now you grow up knowing things a child should not know. There’s a spirit in pornography, there’s a spirit in the dysfunctional houses many of us came up in, and often it begins to afflict you while you’re a child.

DMX told how someone he looked up to laced a blunt with crack when he was fourteen, and asked why would you do that to a child. Then when he bugs out as an adult we laugh and say he’s got to stop smoking that crack. The demons we wrestle with came upon us while we were still children. Many of you were ten, eleven, twelve, thirteen, fourteen years old when you found that porn stash and have not been able to put it away since, because a demonic door was opened to you from that point on.

“And ofttimes it hath cast him into the fire, and into the waters, to destroy him”. The spirit that’s in many of us desires to destroy you.

A brother has a lust in him and a sister has a lust in her: how do they find each other? He looked across the room and lined up and saw her? It has nothing to do with your flesh. The demon in you is saying woohoo to the demon in her on the other side of the room, and her demon is saying woohoo back, and they agree together to be in the midst of fornication. It’s a spiritual thing: the demon in you found a demon in her.

“If thou canst believe, all things are possible to him that believeth.” If you believe, all things are possible.

“Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief.” The father cried out with tears: Lord, you see something in me that I’m lacking, help me. This is why Christ was daily in the temple teaching all those things that benefit us, and one of the things that benefits us is knowing we need help from the Lord.

“He rebuked the foul spirit”. Earlier in the chapter it was called a dumb spirit. The father didn’t know the fullness of what Christ knew: the father only spoke on what he could see, a dumb spirit trying to destroy his son, but Christ said it’s a foul, filthy spirit in that young boy. Hatred is a foul spirit. Evil concupiscence that goes into sodomy is a foul spirit. Envy, porn, bestiality, whatever you want to name it, those are foul spirits. Until you start deeming the spirits within us as foul, you will never get rid of them. Don’t make light of it like the father did. Many of us have to have that same reckoning: it’s a foul, filthy spirit within us.

“Come out of him, and enter no more into him.” You may think you’ve gotten rid of a spirit, but Satan definitely makes a comeback. Look where lustful, evil concupiscence can lead: a man of thirty-eight who killed his sixteen-year-old niece after impregnating her, a man of forty-one who killed his girlfriend’s thirteen-year-old niece after impregnating her. While he was with the so-called girlfriend, who was he really paying attention to? Then to cover up his foul spirit he murdered the young sister. Many of you say, I would never go that far, and Satan says hold my cup. You don’t know yourself, because even the beginning stages of this spirit are foul.

And all you old ass men with beards and back hair, a whole job with a pension package, pulling up to the high school picking up little girls with flowers and balloons: foul spirits. All praises for repentance, but what the scripture is saying is ask the Lord that the spirit don’t come back upon you, because Satan ain’t done until we’re in the ground or Christ comes.

“And the spirit cried, and rent him sore, and came out of him: and he was as one dead”. Paul says I die daily, and when you get rid of those spirits it’s like you’re dying behind it. You think those spirits are going to say, I’m packing my bags, see you later? No. That spirit hangs on to you like somebody dragged out by their feet. It doesn’t want to leave its house. It has been comfortable there since you were a child, warm, fed, everything it needs, and you’re giving it an eviction notice out of the blue because you read it out of a book. That spirit is kicking and screaming. This is war.

“Insomuch that many said, He is dead.” Dying daily ain’t just about you. Everybody has to be able to recognize, wait a minute, that brother was robbing people, being a thief, and he ain’t that guy no more. They have to see that the spirit has died in you. Your death is not a one-person vigil. You are a walking billboard for Christ. None of these things should be named among any of us: put it away, cast it out. You have the power to do it; many times we just don’t use the power the Lord gave us.

“But Jesus took him by the hand, and lifted him up; and he arose.” The disciples asked privately, “Why could not we cast him out?” And Christ said, “This kind can come forth by nothing, but by prayer and fasting.” Christ is saying you are able to do the exact same thing.

Many of us say, I’ve been fasting a long time about this and I still battle with it. Maybe it’s not just how often you fast but the duration of your fast. A lot of brothers have already changed to one meal a day, so fasting for one day is pretty much what you’re already doing. Change the duration: go three days, four days, five days. If you really want that spirit to leave you, there is no extent you won’t go. The white man is a damn liar saying you’re going to die if you don’t drink water for three days. All things can be done through the Lord. Don’t get faint-hearted.

precepts.why:
“Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word.” How do you cleanse yourself from the foul spirit within you, within us? How does a young woman cleanse her ways from the foul spirit within her? It goes right back to the word of God: you cleanse yourself through the word of God.

So be proactive. If you found your mama’s or daddy’s porn stash back in the day and you know that plagues your mind, put those settings on your phone so you can’t go there, and safeguard your spirit. It’s your salvation that’s on the line.

sense.text:
“How is the gold become dim! how is the most fine gold changed!” This is the question Jeremiah asked. Gold is our royal state: above all nations, with the nations paying us tribute. That’s the status of gold. How did the most fine gold change?

“The stones of the sanctuary are poured out in the top of every street.” That fine gold is now poured out, cast out.

“The precious sons of Zion, comparable to fine gold”. Is this talking about Fort Knox? Is it talking about Putin’s stockpile of gold? No, it’s talking about the precious sons of Zion. You are comparable to fine gold.

“How are they esteemed as earthen pitchers”: how are you now in the position of an earthen pitcher, made from the earth? “The work of the hands of the potter!” We are in the hands of the Lord. Remember, his ears are open to the righteous but he is against them that do evil. When we were the fine gold it was because the Lord was with us. We turned against the Lord, now the Lord is fighting against us, and this is the state we’re in now.

precepts.why:
“Only the gold, and the silver, the brass, the iron, the tin, and the lead,” and then: “Every thing that may abide the fire, ye shall make it go through the fire, and it shall be clean”. Everything that may withstand, endure, the fire, God says you shall make it go through the fire. The gold, the silver, the brass, the iron, the tin and the lead must go through the fire in order to be clean. It is not just melting it: the Lord says that for it to be clean it must go through the fire.

“Nevertheless it shall be purified”: it shall be purified by going through the fire. And here’s the thing: you are going through the fire, either willingly or forcefully by the Lord. Either way, you’re going through the fire.

“Son of man, the house of Israel is to me become dross: all they are brass, and tin, and iron, and lead, in the midst of the furnace”. These are the same metals of Numbers 31 that have to go through the fire to be clean. Dross is something regarded as worthless: rubbish, trash. The Lord says Israel has become worthless, like trash, to him. “Because ye are all become dross”: not some, all. In all Israel there is dross, trash, rubbish.

“As they gather silver, and brass, and iron, and lead, and tin, into the midst of the furnace, to blow the fire upon it, to melt it”. Israel is that silver, tin, lead and brass, and he is going to melt you whether you like it or not. So it’s best that you get rid of those things within you yourself. God is going to do it regardless, but if you do it, his ears are open to your prayers. If he has to do it: “so will I gather you in mine anger and in my fury, and I will leave you there, and melt you.” He does it out of anger and fury.

He’s going to melt us down because we are that gold, that silver, those precious things. The Lord is going to get the best product out of us one way or another: either we willingly follow his word, or he purges us from the earth and still gets the result he wants. He wants a sinless congregation. Repenting, becoming newborn babes, seeking the Lord, begging him to help our unbelief, fasting and prayer, whatever is necessary; either that, or the Lord will be the one to melt you, and he’ll do it out of fury: “I will gather you, and blow upon you in the fire of my wrath”, “and ye shall know that I the Lord have poured out my fury upon you.”

Putin’s got gold in Russia, Fort Knox and the Franklin Mint have gold and silver, but the Lord is not talking about that. He’s talking about the gold and silver in the midst of Israel, and he’s going to melt us because, as Numbers 31 says, we need to be made clean.

Sisters, when that lustful spirit is on you and a brother gives you that look across the room, catch yourself and ask why he noticed you out of every woman in there. It’s like turning on a flashlight in the dark: the foul spirit on you is radiating through the whole building, and a brother doesn’t look at you because his beard is glistening. And don’t come complaining about how wicked the one you handpicked is: you handpicked her, you handpicked him. Either you fix it or the Lord fixes it, and he’s going to do it in his fury. Enjoy the fire.

sense.text: “That in all the land, saith the Lord”: all the land of Babylon. “Two parts therein shall be cut off and die; but the third shall be left therein.” Two out of three will be cut off and die.

“And I will bring the third part through the fire”. The Lord constantly deals with bringing us through the fire. He’s going to melt us; we’re like the clay in the potter’s hands, and that whole process deals with fire. Two thirds are going to be killed, and the third part that’s left is going to be brought through the fire. Whether we like it or not, there is going to be fire from the Lord: one to clean us up, the other to kill us. You choose.

Some of the stuff we have to deal with and overcome is embarrassing. You might feel ashamed, like they’re going to look at you this way or that way. You’ve got to get over it if you sincerely want to be cleansed and healed of the spirits that have been on you since you were a child, because if it’s the Lord that has to do it, it’s going to be through fire, his anger and fury.

“And will refine them as silver is refined, and will try them as gold is tried”. It is the same process as being cleaned: he has to get rid of the dross, the trash, the filth within us, and the fire is what’s going to do it. Here it is again: the price of gold. For you to become the gold that is no longer dim, you must go through the fire willingly, or the Lord will do it through his anger and fury. And there is no turning back. Some think, I’m just going to stay outside, I’m not going to come in, I don’t want to go through all the stuff they’re bringing out. Then the fire you’ll receive is being in the two thirds. The children of Israel will go through the fire whether they like it or not; we are not going to avoid what the Lord said is coming upon us in any way, shape, form or fashion.

“They shall call on my name, and I will hear them: I will say, It is my people”. When will the Lord say we are his people? After you have gone through the fire, and that fire begins with you denying yourself, as Christ said. There are going to be things that are uncomfortable, shameful, regretful; we are talking about a sea of people filled with foul spirits. That is why the Lord set up all the Bishops, all the Deacons, the leaders ordained in the various congregations: for the healing of the nation. Sisters, the same for you with the senior sisters. In order to purge it and fix it, you have to acknowledge it.

“And they shall say, The Lord is my God.” We will gladly say the Lord is my God, but some of us say it with contingencies: he’s your God as long as you ain’t going through nothing, and when you start catching hell it’s, Lord, why have you forsaken me, Lord, am I even an Israelite?

“And I will punish the world for their evil, and the wicked for their iniquity; and I will cause the arrogancy of the proud to cease”. Now the Lord goes into taking down the nations: he’s going to take down Esau. “And will lay low the haughtiness of the terrible”: there is no one on earth more terrible than the so-called white man.

And some of y’all lust after him. Some of that porn you’re watching is because you’re lusting after the white man or the white woman. That is your lust, that foul spirit.

“I will make a man more precious than fine gold”. The Lord is giving a promise, and his word is true. “Even a man than the golden wedge of Ophir.” Ophir was known for gold of a quality superior to all other lands.

“Therefore I will shake the heavens”: for this reason, because his plans are to make you finer than the gold of the land of Ophir, he will shake the heavens, meaning war and destruction. “And the earth shall remove out of her place”. Because the Lord loves you, because you’re the apple of his eye, he’s willing to bring destruction on the earth and make the earth shift its axis in order to bring you back to being the fine gold you fell from.

“In the wrath of the Lord of hosts, and in the day of his fierce anger.” This goes right back to the fierce anger we read in Ezekiel. The judgment and the fire coming upon the earth is to purify you, the fine gold. The fire to make you clean and purified, or the fire to destroy you, is coming whether you like it or not, and you choose. So we need to be praying and fasting, begging the Lord to help our unbelief, going to the Lord and going to the elders to get fixed, because the fire to purge us, either from our sins or from the earth, is coming.

precepts.why:
Remember what we just read: “two parts therein shall be cut off and die; but the third shall be left therein. And I will bring the third part through the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined, and will try them as gold is tried”. The Lord says he’s going to do it whether you like it or not. Focus on those words: I will.

“They shall call on my name, and I will hear them: I will say, It is my people: and they shall say, The Lord is my God.” That is how he makes a man more precious than fine gold: he refines him through the fire, and then he hears us and calls us his people.

sense.text:
“But the day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night”. There’s that four-letter word again: will. It shall come to pass. “In the which the heavens shall pass away with a great noise”: a thermonuclear noise, a bomb. In Isaiah 13 he said he will shake the heavens, and here Peter says the same thing. The prophets and the apostles didn’t say anything different.

“And the elements shall melt with fervent heat”. Didn’t we read in Numbers 31 that the gold and silver have to go through the fire to be made clean? The Lord says this land has to be melted with fervent heat, and this land is filled with people. In Ezekiel 22 the Lord said, I will melt you. The day of the Lord is going to come and everything is going to melt with fervent heat, and in that time one of two things happens: deliverance or destruction.

“Seeing then that all these things shall be dissolved, what manner of persons ought ye to be in all holy conversation and godliness”. It goes right back to where the class began: conversation, no guile, no evil speaking. Destruction is coming upon the earth, so pay attention that there’s no guile in you, no evil speaking in you. Our conversation has to be right; the prophets said it and the apostles said the same thing. You’re repented, a newborn babe, born again, so you know this is what’s coming. What does that mean? Get yourself right.

“Looking for and hasting unto the coming of the day of God”. We’re dealing with bill collectors, broke backs, broke knees, headaches, migraines, dehydration, emotional men and masculine women, and the list goes on. How much longer should we continue in that? We’re in captivity, so you should want the day of the Lord, the time of our rulership, to hasten.

“Wherein the heavens being on fire shall be dissolved”. There are people in a heavenly place over us, and we, as earthen pitchers, are like the ground. This is us currently. I don’t care what your tax bracket is, where you live or if your community is gated: a Karen is watching you through the window right now, and she put the for-sale sign in her yard as soon as you got out of that moving truck. The Lord calls those ruling over us the heavens, in the sense that they’re in a high estate, and he is going to burn them up. Their rulership shall be dissolved. This is why you haste for the day of God: you’re finally going to see your oppressor cease.

“Nevertheless we, according to his promise, look for new heavens and a new earth”: new rulership, and finally our own land. “Wherein dwelleth righteousness”, meaning there will be no more foul spirits. The foul spirits we battle with, either we purge them or we will be purged, because that foul spirit cannot enter in. The foul spirit hanging on to us, renting us sore so that we look like we’re dead when we purge it, will not enter in. If that foul spirit is in you, you won’t enter in.

“Be diligent that ye may be found of him in peace”: found by Christ in peace. We don’t miss those foul spirits no more, we don’t miss being slaves, we don’t miss being on the bottom. “Without spot”: that’s the dross we went over, in the gold: the trash, the rubbish, the filth, the worthlessness and uselessness within the gold. “And blameless”: that none of us be found as murderers or busybodies in other men’s business. The entire blueprint has been laid down, so when the day of the Lord is upon us we can’t be clueless.

“And men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil.” Men love the foul spirits within them rather than getting right. Paul was open about what he battled, and one of the things the Lord set up the leadership for is the healing of the nation, so we shouldn’t keep things bottled up.

“For every one that doeth evil hateth the light, neither cometh to the light”. The Lord set up leaders many years ago, a lot of them longer than some of us have been alive. Schizophreniform includes social withdrawal, not operating well in social settings, but here it says there’s a foul spirit in you that will make you not come to where Christ is. It’s not you being an introvert. You have to purge the foul spirit from you. When the leaders are in the various cities or in your local city, there are always ones who are there in body but not there in spirit, because what is leading them is the foul spirit that hates the light.

“Lest his deeds should be reproved.” Why do we keep things bottled up inside? Because you don’t want the correction for the foul spirit within you. The light is going to illuminate that spirit, and we don’t want our deeds revealed; we don’t want to deal with the shame and the embarrassment. Why do they always have to bring such and such up? To get your mind right. You better thank the Lord for the righteous smiting you, and count it as the ointment that was upon Aaron’s beard.

“But he that doeth truth cometh to the light”. The brothers who want to get right come around. When leadership is at the table going through scriptures, or in the war room, you see brothers asking sincere questions and getting the understanding. And some brothers never come around. You’re trying to hide the foul spirit within you, but when you try to hide it, all you do is illuminate it and make it more obvious.

“That his deeds may be made manifest, that they are wrought in God.” The objective of coming around, despite the correction and the instruction, is that you want it daily. That is what we started with: Christ daily in the temple, and the Lord who daily loadeth us with benefits.

Either way the gold is going to be purged, whether you like it or not. “For there shall be in every place”: not some places, every place. The purifying process, getting rid of the dross, the trash, the filth, is going to come upon you no matter where you are. In those days, what manner of man or woman shall you be found to be?

“A great insurrection upon those that fear the Lord.” You can compare this to the fire the Lord said we must go through. Before the insurrection you fear the Lord, and that is how they know who you are. The Bishop went over this years ago, and multiple times, with the Spanish Inquisition: they watched and observed, they knew who kept the Sabbath, who circumcised their children, they already knew all of that. They came to confirm it, to see if you would forsake the Lord. That trial, that fire, is coming to clean and purify you whether you like it or not: one is for salvation’s sake, to be found among them that fear the Lord, and the other is to purge you from the earth.

“They shall be like mad men, sparing none, but still spoiling and destroying those that fear the Lord.” If you have not really meditated on this time which is to come, start doing so, and ask the Lord to help our unbelief, because what we want in that time is deliverance. Those who are keeping the commandments are who their main focus will be upon: “For they shall waste and take away their goods, and cast them out of their houses.”

“Then shall they be known, who are my chosen”. Remember we read that the Lord will say it is my people, and we will say the Lord is my God. The only way his chosen, the elect, are known is going through the fire. “And they shall be tried as the gold in the fire.” In a few verses Ezra breaks down what the price of gold is: it is you. You are the price of gold.

“Hear, O ye my beloved, saith the Lord”. You would think God hates us, that God is against us during that time, and this is the point of keeping the faith: God says no, my beloved, because he already has a kingdom prepared for you and rulership set for you. All you have to do is go through this chastening and the fire.

“Behold, the days of trouble are at hand, but I will deliver you from the same.” There’s that four-letter word again: will. God said he will deliver us.

“Be ye not afraid, neither doubt”. That’s why the brother in Mark 9 asked the Lord to help his unbelief: that is what doubt is. The entire Bible lines up with itself, no matter who is saying it. Don’t let anybody make you think Paul is saying something contrary to Christ, or Peter contrary to Paul, or the apostles contrary to the prophets. Christianity contradicts the Bible.

“And the guide of them who keep my commandments and precepts, saith the Lord God”. God is the guide only of them who keep his commandments. The people that forsook the commandments and forsook God will go about aimlessly looking for hope, for direction, for instructions, while you brothers and sisters who keep the commandments of God have a guide.

“Let not your sins weigh you down, and let not your iniquities lift up themselves.” It goes right back to everything taught this class: the evil conversation, the evil concupiscence, all the foul spirits within us. We must purge them, that they don’t weigh us down.
